viewer_sees: a blood-red eclipsed moon above the walls and palace terraces of Nineveh at night; on the palace roof two scholars in long fringed robes look up, one clutching a clay tablet
the Nineveh throne room: a rough-handed commoner sits stiffly on the king's throne in the royal robe and crown while courtiers bow; from a dark doorway at the left edge the real king watches
the palace roof under a dense field of stars: three scholars with clay tablets and styluses copy what they see in the sky, a low brazier glowing between them
the moon close and huge: the dark shadow has bitten deep into its disc, the rest glowing blood-red, a thin ring of light at its edge

PROCESS / CUTAWAY — the moon disc drawn as a scholar's diagram on clay: four quarters, each tied by a thin line to a land at the frame edge (Akkad south, Elam east, Amurru west, Subartu north); the eclipse shadow creeps across one quarter
the king of Assyria on his throne lifts his eyes to a high window where the eclipsed moon hangs dark red; the window's red light falls across him like a shadow
MACRO OBJECT — a scholar's hands turn a clay omen tablet away from the king's cylinder seal toward an empty second stool; the red eclipse moon trembles small in a bowl of water beside it
Esarhaddon, king of Assyria, stands between the carved winged human-headed bulls of his palace gate: curled beard, tall royal cap, fringed robe, a mace in hand
LEDGER — the royal archive at Nineveh: hundreds of small clay letter-tablets packed in shelves and reed baskets, a scribe adding still more until a basket spills over
Esarhaddon steps down from his throne and walks out through a dark doorway at the left; the throne stands empty behind him, the red moon in the high window
the stand-in is prepared — washed with water, anointed with oil from a horn, dressed by attendants in the king's robe → enthroned, a young veiled woman seated beside him as his queen
before the winged sun-disc of Shamash on an altar at dawn, a scholar recites from a clay tablet; the substitute king on his throne bows his head as if taking a weight onto his shoulders
a scholar kneels and ties a small inscribed clay tablet with cord into the fringed hem of the substitute's robe
the real king hidden in a small inner chamber of the palace, in a plain wool tunic with no crown, reading a clay letter by one lamp while a messenger kneels at the door
close on wet clay: a scribe's stylus presses the first wedges of a letter's opening line, finished lines above it

TIMELINE — the substitute on the throne seen through the same high window night after night, the moon passing through its phases, a tally of strokes on a clay tablet in the foreground growing toward a hundred
EMPTY AFTERMATH — the throne empty in grey dawn light, the royal robe folded on its seat, a single cup on the step; no person anywhere
three men stand in a palace courtyard before the chief exorcist: a chained condemned criminal, a foreign prisoner of war, a laborer with a basket of bricks; the exorcist's hand lifts to choose
Akkad in Babylonia: at the steps of a mud-brick temple, young Damqi in a fine fringed Babylonian robe stands beside his father, the temple's high official in white linen
the king's agent in Babylonia, a grey-bearded Assyrian official, writes his report into a clay tablet by lamplight, a clay envelope waiting beside it
Damqi enthroned in Akkad in the king's robe and crown, his young queen beside him, both solemn and very still; scholars and guards at the edges of the hall
a royal burial chamber: two shrouded figures lie in state on biers under embroidered cloths with gold ornaments, lamps around them, mourning women with raised arms and loosened hair
before the ritual: a prophetess with loose hair at a temple doorway grips young Damqi's wrist and points past him toward the palace
MACRO OBJECT — the crown Damqi wore, resting on a folded royal robe at the edge of the bier, one lamp flame beside it
Esarhaddon, back in his throne room, holds the report tablet while his scholars bow low before him; his face unreadable
an old scholar guides a boy apprentice copying an eclipse omen from a worn, ancient tablet onto fresh clay; shelves of old tablets behind them
summer heat: a scholar marks a day on a clay calendar tablet; through the doorway behind him guards lead a new stand-in, a laborer, toward the throne room
ANIMATED MAP — an old map in clay tones: the Assyrian army column marches from Nineveh toward Egypt; partway there the king's banner tilts and falls
a Babylonian chronicle tablet close, dense cuneiform columns → the walled city of Isin on its plain a thousand years earlier, temple tower, palm groves and canals

Isin: King Erra-imitti leads his gardener Enlil-bani, a weathered man with a pruning knife at his belt, in from the palace garden → places the royal tiara on the gardener's head as he sits on the throne
Erra-imitti in his own palace chamber raises a steaming bowl of hot soup to his lips with both hands, a servant behind him with the jug
Enlil-bani on the throne with the tiara on his head, gardener's hands gripping the throne arms; courtiers hesitate at the edges of the hall
one of Enlil-bani's own inscriptions: a clay foundation cone covered in cuneiform, half-buried in the earth of a ruined wall
the city wall of Isin being rebuilt: workers carry mud bricks up ladders, Enlil-bani in the tiara watching from the rampart
LEDGER — a threshing floor: of five heaps of barley one used to go to the tax scribe; now ten heaps stand and only one is carried off, the farmer keeping the rest
SILHOUETTE — black against a dusk sky, a figure in a tiara stands on the palace wall, spear silhouettes of armed men gathering around him
EMPTY AFTERMATH — in Nineveh, the substitute's royal robe lies folded on a bare bench in the corner; deep behind it the real king sits on his throne again, small and far
Isin: the shrouded bier of Erra-imitti carried out at the left; on the right the gardener sits crowned on the throne and the whole court kneels to him
two crowns side by side: the Assyrian royal cap on a folded robe in shadow, the Isin tiara in light beside a gardener's pruning knife → END CARD: poster of the whole story with title and SUBSCRIBE
